owner_calls.question: In Agent Carter S2#9 Thompson double-crosses Sousa and Carter (delays them, then holds them at gunpoint so he can blow up the gamma cannon and kill Frost, Masters and Wilkes) before they are back on the same side in S2#10. Should this betrayal get its own stage after S2#8?
options: Add a stage at Agent Carter S2#9 (kind ally): Thompson turns on Sousa and Peggy Carter and holds them at gunpoint to blow up the gamma cannon with Frost inside.
Leave as is: a one-episode double-cross inside the same team-up, with no lasting turn
owner_calls.evidence: Wikipedia's S2#9 summary: 'Thompson then turns on Carter and Sousa, delaying them, as he actually intends to remote detonate the cannon to kill Frost, Masters, and Wilkes... Thompson holds the others at gunpoint until his signal is un-jammed.' In S2#10 they work together again and Thompson gives Carter the Council key.

owner_calls.question: Cull Obsidian and Gamora never share a scene: Gamora is with Thanos on Knowhere and Vormir while Cull is on Earth. The only link is that both are Thanos's adopted children (the film's 'Children of Thanos'). Is being adopted siblings enough for a connection under the explicit-and-meaningful rule?
options: Keep: being adopted siblings is an explicit family link
Drop the connection (N7): they never interact on screen
owner_calls.evidence: In Infinity War, Cull goes to Earth (Greenwich Village, Wakanda) and Gamora stays with Thanos (Knowhere, Sanctuary II, Vormir). MCU wiki: Cull was 'one of Thanos' adopted children'. Wikipedia: the film calls the henchmen the 'Children of Thanos'.
